mechanism_claims.claim_text: CF-labelled HBD4 analogs enter bacterial and fungal cells and accumulate intracellularly; the paper interprets killing as involving membrane perturbation plus intracellular accumulation rather than simple membrane lysis alone.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: H4-1d, H4-2d, and H4-3d CF-labelled analogs
mechanism_claims.limitations: Localization and morphology are direct imaging evidence for interaction/internalization; they do not identify a single molecular intracellular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Membrane interaction is supported by FM4-64/PI microscopy and model lipid vesicle binding; the paper reports membrane defects in microbes but no simple diffusion across model vesicles.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model vesicle binding and microbial membrane perturbation support membrane interaction but do not prove a pore-only mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper proposes multiple downstream targets after cytosolic accumulation, including possible binding to anionic molecules such as nucleic acids; this remains an inferred mechanism context rather than direct target identification.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct nucleic-acid-binding assay or specific intracellular target assay is reported in the local source material.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Mechanism is bounded to membrane perturbation/internalization and inferred downstream intracellular effects.
S2 Fig provides qualitative CCCP/PMF activity context as an image; no exact chart values were promoted to row-level records.
